# CegarPlay

> A static browser playground for CEGAR loops (counterexample-guided abstraction refinement)
> written in answer set programming, solved with clingo 5.8.1 (with Lua) compiled to WebAssembly.
> A project is one JSON file: ASP fragments, a loop script, and settings.

## Docs

- [Technical manual](manual.md): the complete reference: project format, ASP conventions
  (glue/1, relevant/1, #program refine(k), clause/3), the loop language with its grammar and
  error messages, templates, the Lua runtime API, settings, outcomes, events, troubleshooting,
  and a workflow for agents.
- [Tutorial](tutorial.html): lessons for people, as an HTML fragment (shown in the page's
  Tutorial tab).
- [Design guide](guide/index.html): twelve pages on designing CEGAR loops (abstraction, check,
  relevant/1, soundness testing, loop shapes, rule refinements, cores, optimisation), each step
  an example of the library group "guide"; page 12 has a checklist of all its rules.

- Specifications of the newer parts: [instances, generators, campaigns, fuzz, pools](docs/spec-instances.md),
  [recordings](docs/spec-recording.md), [audit, certificates, lift, proof logs](docs/spec-soundness.md),
  [domain views, candidate space, cursor](docs/spec-views.md). The page's tabs: Instances (9),
  Campaign (10), Observatory (11).

## Examples

- [Loops from the literature](manual.md#loops-from-the-literature): MaxHS, MARCO, OLL, Benders,
  CEGIS, AReQS, RAReQS, CAQE, branch-and-check (`on partial`), omission-based abstraction, each mapped to a loop pattern and an
  example id (tags `ihs`, `marco`, `oll`, `benders`, `cegis`, `rareqs`, `caqe`, `omission`).
- [Library manifest](examples/library.json): every example with id, group, summary, loop shape
  and expected solution count. Each example is the project file `examples/<id>.json`.
- Open an example in the page: `index.html?example=<id>`; add `&tab=4` for the loop script,
  `&manual=true&tab=8` for the manual.

## Running without a browser

- `node tools/run.mjs <project.json | library id> [-c name=value] [--solutions N|all] [--json]`
  validates and runs a project with the same engine as the page (needs the repository and Node).
- `python3 tools/cegarcheck.py <project.json> [--mode block] [--solutions all] [--instance id] [--variant name]` runs a project
  with Python clingo (one abstraction, one check, one link); compare with `--mode block`.
- `node tools/run.mjs` and `node tools/audit.mjs` take `--instance id` and `--variant name` too.
- `node tools/audit.mjs <id>` audits a loop (sound / unsound with a witness); `node tools/run.mjs <id> --proof log.jsonl`
  then `python3 tools/certcheck.py <project.json> log.jsonl` certifies a solution count;
  `node tools/bench.mjs <id> --suite NAME` runs a campaign suite.

## Contributing examples

- Put a project with a top-level `library` block in `examples/contrib/` (see
  `examples/contrib/README.md`), then `node tools/make-examples.mjs`.
